description: Find true priorities by testing each spending line against one question. If you had one hundred dollars more, would you spend it here, and if you had one hundred dollars less, would you cut it here. Rank every line by marginal value and move dollars toward what matters. Works for personal budgets and departmental allocation.

steps.description: Build a complete list of current spending lines for the period.

inputs.desc: The budget or allocation being examined and its purpose

inputs.name: time-period
inputs.desc: The period the spending covers, such as a month, quarter, or year

outputs.name: spend-inventory
outputs.desc: Every recurring and one-time outflow grouped by category

outputs.name: baseline-totals
outputs.desc: Current total by category and overall

process: List every recurring and one-time outflow for the period.
Group the outflows by category.
Record the current amount for each line and total it.

steps.description: For each line, test whether one hundred more dollars would improve the outcome.

inputs.name: spend-inventory
inputs.desc: The grouped list of spending lines

outputs.name: add-value-scores
outputs.desc: Benefit score for adding a marginal hundred dollars to each line

outputs.name: high-add-lines
outputs.desc: Lines where more money clearly improves the outcome

process: For each line, estimate the benefit of adding a marginal hundred dollars.
Score the benefit from none to high.
Flag the lines where more money clearly helps.

steps.description: For each line, test whether one hundred fewer dollars would be felt.

inputs.name: spend-inventory
inputs.desc: The grouped list of spending lines

inputs.name: baseline-totals
inputs.desc: Current totals for sizing a cut

outputs.name: cut-pain-scores
outputs.desc: Pain score for removing a marginal hundred dollars from each line

outputs.name: low-pain-lines
outputs.desc: Lines where a cut would barely be felt

process: For each line, estimate the pain of removing a marginal hundred dollars.
Score the pain from none to severe.
Flag the lines where a cut would barely be felt.

steps.description: Combine add value and cut pain into a single priority ranking.

inputs.name: add-value-scores
inputs.desc: Benefit scores from the add-dollar test

inputs.name: cut-pain-scores
inputs.desc: Pain scores from the cut-dollar test

outputs.name: priority-ranking
outputs.desc: Lines ranked from highest to lowest marginal priority

outputs.name: reallocation-candidates
outputs.desc: Top lines to fund and bottom lines to trim

process: Compute a marginal priority for each line from its add value against its cut pain.
Sort the lines from highest to lowest priority.
Mark the top candidates to fund and the bottom candidates to trim.

steps.description: Move dollars from low-priority lines to high-priority lines.

inputs.name: reallocation-candidates
inputs.desc: Lines to fund and lines to trim

inputs.name: high-add-lines
inputs.desc: Lines where added money helps most

outputs.name: reallocation-plan
outputs.desc: Sized moves of dollars from trims to additions

outputs.name: net-change-summary
outputs.desc: Net change per category after the moves

process: Match dollars freed from low-pain cuts against high-value additions.
Size each move so the total stays within the baseline.
Summarize the net change per category.

steps.description: Write the decision record for the reallocation.

inputs.name: reallocation-plan
inputs.desc: The sized moves of dollars

inputs.name: priority-ranking
inputs.desc: The ranking behind the moves

outputs.name: marginal-analysis-report
outputs.desc: One-page record of the ranking and the moves

outputs.name: decision-log
outputs.desc: Which lines were funded, held, or trimmed and why

process: Document the ranking and the reasoning for each move.
Record which lines were funded, held, or trimmed.
Produce the one-page summary for sign-off.

description: Optimize when money moves rather than how much. Map inflows and outflows by date across ninety days, find the valleys and peaks in the balance, shift movable outflows and pull receivables earlier, then value the smoother timing as float.

outputs.name: cash-sources

process: Total the cash across accounts available without penalty.
Note any committed funds that are not truly available.
Record the as-of date for the count.

steps.description: Compute the net monthly burn rate.

process: Total the monthly outflows across fixed and variable costs.
Subtract any reliable monthly inflow to get the net burn.
Break the burn down by category.

Convert the result to months of runway.
Mark the date the cash runs out at the current rate.

Recompute the runway if a major expense hits.
Recompute the runway if the timeline to profitability doubles.

description: Find the costs that never appear on a statement. Some cheap options are expensive once every cost is counted.

Record the sticker price of each option as its visible cost.
